$why: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the media_analyses component namespace.
Registering ONE analysis component used to require editing a dozen places that
each privately encoded 'how many analysis components exist', none of them
referencing any other: a CHECK constraint, a stored procedure's guard, that
procedure's per-component byte cap, a hand-picked migration list in a workflow,
four staging-integration phase scripts, and four TypeScript sites. Nothing
compared them, so a disagreement surfaced only as a staging matrix failure ~40
minutes in, naming a symptom rather than the cause.
check_analysis_components.mjs reads THIS file and fails the build when any of
those sites disagrees with it. Change a component here first, then make the
sites agree; the guard tells you which ones you missed, in seconds, offline.
THE CAP TRAP, which is why maxResultBytes is declared per component rather than
left implicit: editor_record_analysis picks its cap with a CASE whose `else`
branch is 16384 bytes. A component added without its own branch SILENTLY
inherits 16 KiB, and `component_too_large` is PERMANENT — there is no retry.
The guard computes what the CASE would actually return for every component and
compares it to the value declared here, so an inherited default has to be a
decision somebody wrote down rather than an accident nobody noticed.
$axes: digestKeyed      — editor_record_analysis writes it, keyed by component digest.
consumedByDirector — editorDirector passes its evidence into the Director call.
THESE ARE NOT THE SAME SET, and conflating them is a real hazard. A component
can be STORABLE before anything READS it: that is the deliberate state the
build plan describes for alignment, which lists 'wiring it' and 'consuming it'
as separate items and warns that landing it half-wired would be worse than not
landing it. Declaring the two axes separately makes 'recorded but not yet
consumed' something somebody wrote down, rather than a site everyone forgot.
$recordAnalysisDefaultCapBytes: The `else` branch of editor_record_analysis's cap CASE. Declared so the guard can compute each component's EFFECTIVE cap and catch one silently inheriting it.
$stagingMigrationBaseline: The staging matrix applies a HAND-PICKED list of migrations, not everything in
supabase/migrations/. Migrations at or below this number reached staging before
that list existed and are assumed present. Any migration ABOVE it that touches
the component contract must appear in the workflow's apply list, or the matrix
runs against a schema that does not match the checkout — which is how 0100
failed, as something that looked unrelated.
